{{Current events|year=2019|month=02|day=22|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2019 Venezuelan presidential crisis]]
**[[Venezuelan National Guard]] (GNB) troops open fire on a group of indigenous [[Pemon]] protesters that attempted to block a military convoy heading to the [[Brazil–Venezuela border]], killing at least two people and wounding 14 others, several seriously. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/the_americas/one-dead-multiple-injured-after-venezuelan-national-guard-opens-fire-on-opposition-supporters/2019/02/22/09d60f1a-3518-11e9-8375-e3dcf6b68558_story.html?utm_term=.a6e407ea2afc (''The Washington Post'')] [https://www.miamiherald.com/news/nation-world/world/americas/venezuela/article226624859.html (''Miami Herald'')]
*[[American-led intervention in the Syrian Civil War]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] agrees to keep about 400 U.S. troops in [[Syria]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/02/22/politics/syria-us-troops-donald-trump/index.html (CNN)]

;Arts and culture
*[[Crisis in Venezuela]]
**The [[Venezuela Aid Live]] [[benefit concert]] takes place on the [[Colombia–Venezuela border]]. The all-day event on the Colombian side of the [[Tienditas Bridge]] is expected to attract up to 250,000 people. [https://www.thejournal.ie/venezuela-live-aid-4506922-Feb2019/ (''The Journal'')]
**In response to the concert, [[Nicolás Maduro]] announces a [[Venezuela Aid Live#Maduro response|rival concert]] on the Venezuelan side of the border, and state-owned [[Venezolana de Televisión]] reports 150 artists will participate, but no artists are signed. [https://www.billboard.com/articles/columns/latin/8499591/hands-off-venezuela-concert-150-artists (Billboard)]
**[[Venezuela]]n interim President [[Juan Guaidó]] arrives at the Venezuela Aid Live concert in [[Cúcuta]], [[Colombia]], defying a travel ban placed on him by the Maduro regime. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2019-02-22/guaido-arrives-at-colombia-benefit-gig-defying-maduro-travel-ban (Bloomberg)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[List of earthquakes in 2019]]
**A magnitude 7.5 earthquake hits [[Ecuador]], near the border with [[Peru]]. It is relatively deep, with a depth of {{convert|152|km|mi|abbr=on}}. [https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/eventpage/at00pnbol0/executive (USGS)]
*Flooding is reported throughout [[Tennessee]] amid heavy rain. Rain is expected to continue, possibly making the flooding worse. [https://www.wsmv.com/news/flooding-already-reported-in-several-counties-in-middle-tennessee/article_4147cb50-36c1-11e9-b1ca-6b7e6af2d215.html (WSMV)]

;Law and crime
*[[R. Kelly#Alleged sexual abuse of minors|R. Kelly sexual abuse case]]
**American musician [[R. Kelly]] is indicted for raping a minor. A judge in Cook County, Illinois, issues an arrest warrant for Kelly in regard to 10 counts of aggravated criminal sexual abuse. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/02/22/entertainment/r-kelly-indictment/index.html (CNN)] [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/r-kelly-charged-multiple-counts-sexual-abuse-minor-n974621 (NBC News)]
*[[New England Patriots]] owner [[Robert Kraft]] is charged in a prostitution sting in the U.S. state of Florida. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/02/22/sports/robert-kraft-jupiter-orchids-arrest.html (New York Times)] [https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/patriots/2019/02/22/robert-kraft-florida-prostitution-sting-what-we-know/2951063002/ (USA Today)]

;Politics and elections
*[[History of the Labour Party (UK)|History of the UK Labour Party]], [[Antisemitism in the UK Labour Party]]
**[[United Kingdom|British]] [[Member of Parliament (United Kingdom)|MP]] [[Ian Austin (politician)|Ian Austin]] quits [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] over a "culture of extremism, anti-semitism and intolerance" within the party under [[Jeremy Corbyn]], becoming the ninth Labour MP to quit this week. However, unlike the others, he will not be joining [[The Independent Group]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2019/feb/22/labour-mp-ian-austin-quits-the-party (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2019 North Korea–United States Hanoi Summit]]
**The [[Presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] weighs softening demands ahead of the second summit meeting with [[List of leaders of North Korea|North Korean leader]] [[Kim Jong-un]] in [[Hanoi]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/02/22/politics/trump-demands-north-korea-summit/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Sudanese protests (2018–19)]]
**[[President of Sudan|Sudanese President]] [[Omar al-Bashir]] declares a year-long [[state of emergency]], dissolves his [[Cabinet of Sudan|Cabinet]] and sacks all state governors amid ongoing anti-government protests. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-47330423 (BBC)]
*[[Political appointments by Donald Trump]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] nominates [[List of ambassadors of the United States to Canada|U.S. Ambassador to Canada]] [[Kelly Knight Craft]] to be the new [[United States Ambassador to the United Nations|U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/02/22/politics/trump-nomination-un-ambassador-kelly-knight-craft/index.html (CNN)]
